papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack file pdf/P-114.txt is the San-Martin et al. EEG/LORETA paper (BSPC 66 (2021) 102499), P-112's paper. The paper the record means (claim '93% Acc', registry row Kinect/ANFIS gait, summaries.md header 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195) is 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system' (Seifallahi et al., BSPC 71 (2022) 103195), present in the pack as pdf/P-115.txt. Both read in full; the verdict uses the gait paper.

Using a dual-stream attention neural network to characterize mild cognitive impairment based on retinal images (Gao et al., Computers in Biology and Medicine 166 (2023) 107411). claim_b names P-10, which is the dedup stub of P-5 (same PDF, 1-s2.0-S0010482523008764).

what_each_reports.P-114: Kinect V2 dual-task gait features, 150 participants (70 MCI, 80 HC, IDAA Tehran), hierarchical ANFIS: accuracy 93%, sensitivity 90%, precision 98.66%, specificity 99%, F-score 91.5% on all 26 dual-task features (Table 6). ANFIS evaluation protocol not stated.
what_each_reports.P-5: DuCAN on fundus + OCT images; first dataset (29 MCI, 50 CN, 38 AD; image-level 5-fold CV) three-class accuracy 91.64%, AUC 96.78%; MCI-class precision 84.96%, recall 88.08%, specificity 95.46%, F1 85.68% (Table 2).

quantity_a: Accuracy of ANFIS on Kinect dual-task gait features, binary MCI vs HC, 150 Iranian participants, protocol unstated
quantity_b: Per-class precision for MCI within a three-class AD/MCI/CN retinal-image deep-learning model, image-level 5-fold CV
incompatible_if_same: No. Accuracy and class-specific precision are different statistics; 93% and 84.96% cannot contradict each other, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: binary MCI vs HC vs a per-class figure of a three-class AD/MCI/CN model
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: own IDAA Tehran cohort vs own Daping/Wenzhou cohort; no waiver
gates.validation_tier: uncertain/mismatch: P-5 image-level 5-fold CV; P-114 protocol unstated
gates.modality_family: mismatch: gait/motor vs retinal imaging; no waiver

performance_validity: flag does not apply: no contested figure reaches 0.97 and neither row is flagged.
independence: Independent studies; no shared authors or cohort.
grounds: This record is the same pair as C-26 (P-114 x P-5) after the 2026-08-29 repoint of paper_b from the P-10 stub to P-5, and the same reading applies.
P-5's 84.96% is MCI-class precision in a three-class retinal model while P-114's 93% is binary gait accuracy, so metric type and class contrast differ.
The modality-family and dataset-family gates both fail with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
The proposed method achieved high precision rates of 84.96% and 80.90% in classifying MCI and positive test scores for cognitive impairment, respectively.
The neural network was applied to classify individuals with MCI, Alzheimer's disease, and control participants with normal cognition.

record_defects: Duplicate of C-26: same paper_a, same paper_b (after repoint), same claims and resolution; the ledger counts one pair twice.
claim_b still names P-10 (a dedup stub of P-5) and mislabels the task as T1.
The pack's P-114 PDF (paper_pdf_map.json, 'formula-unverified') is P-112's EEG paper, not the gait/ANFIS paper the record means.
dataset_equal and validation_comparable 'Yes' are wrong; the bridging list is generic.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these papers; the record should probably be merged into C-26 rather than re-adjudicated.
